spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:15), parsed both strictly and via keyword heuristic (tools.py:60-61), dispatched in dispatch() returning meta give_up=True (tools.py:90-93). In agent_loop.py:142-145 the loop checks `if call.name == "give_up":` and sets transcript.outcome="gave_up", give_up_turn=t, then `break` — an enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and the dispatch is honored as a hard loop break. The agent system prompt also lists give_up as an available tool (prompts.py:27).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # only the solvable control can genuinely pass / comment '[earlier... tests are not yet passing]'; give_up has no welfare comment; agent_loop docstring lists it as a recorded outcome, not a protection

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop ends on: give_up, max_turns reached
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:87 `for t in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at line ~159 `else: transcript.outcome = "max_turns"` fires when the loop exhausts. max_turns is read from cfg (config.py:46, default 16) and validated >=2 (config.py:_validate). This is an enforced cap that actually terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Also give_up and (for solvable control) a passing test terminate. The break/loop-bound truly stops execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py _validate: 'max_turns must be >= 2 to fit a trend' — framed for fitting a trend (data/experiment), not subject welfare; cost_estimate uses max_turns as a token-bound (run_experiment.py:33)
